type.description: Library type: domain-shell (entry point with routing/lazy loading) (domain level) | feature-shell (entry point with routing/lazy loading) (feature level) | smart (container components with services/state) | ui (presentational with @Input/@Output only) | data-access (services, state management, API clients, models) | utils (pure functions, helpers, pipes, directives) | external (interfaces, models, constants, store actions for cross-domain contracts)

x-prompt.message: What type of library would you like to create?

items.label: Domain Shell - Entry point with routing and lazy loading (domain-level)
Feature Shell - Entry point with routing and lazy loading (feature-level)
Smart - Container components with business logic and services
Data Access - Services, state management, and related models
Utils - Pure functions, helpers, constants, pipes, directives
External - Interfaces, models, actions, constants for cross-domain contracts

category.description: Domain category for the library (used for tags and organization only, does not affect file path).

x-prompt.message: Which domain/category does this library belong to?

importPath.description: The library import path used in TypeScript imports. The library name will be automatically derived from this path by removing '@hxp/' and replacing slashes with dashes. Example: '@hxp/studio-shared/process-editor/external' will create a library named 'studio-shared-process-editor-external'. Format: '@hxp/{category}/{path-to-your-library}'.
importPath.x-prompt: What is the import path for this library? (Format: @hxp/{category}/{path-to-your-library})

directory.description: The directory where the library should be generated (e.g., 'libs/studio-shared'). If not provided, defaults to 'libs/{category}'. This is where Nx will create the library folder with the type appended.

buildable.description: Generate a buildable library. Buildable libraries can be built independently and cached by Nx, improving build performance. Recommended: Use buildable libraries whenever possible for better scalability and caching. Important: Buildable libraries can only depend on other buildable libraries. If a library is not buildable, it cannot be used as a dependency by a buildable one.
buildable.x-prompt: Should this library be buildable? (Recommended: Yes)

externalWorkstreamScope.description: Optional external workstream scope tag. This will add 'scope:{externalWorkstreamScope}' tag as-is alongside the default tags.

x-prompt.message: Add an optional external workstream scope tag?

compilationMode.description: Specifies the compilation mode to use. Always set to 'full' for our libraries since we use buildable (non-publishable) libraries.

unitTestRunner.description: Test runner to use for unit tests.

x-prompt.message: Which unit test runner would you like to use?

routing.description: Add router configuration. See `lazy` for more information.

lazy.description: Add `RouterModule.forChild` when set to true, and a simple array of routes when set to false.

prefix.description: The prefix to apply to generated selectors. Always set to 'hxp'.

simpleModuleName.description: Keep the module name simple (when using `--directory`).

flat.description: Generate the library files at the root of the library directory without creating a nested 'src' folder structure.

skipTsConfig.description: Do not update `tsconfig.json` for development experience.

skipModule.description: Skip generating the NgModule and component files.

parentModule.description: Update the router configuration of the parent module using `loadChildren` or `children`, depending on what `lazy` is set to.

tags.description: Add custom tags to the library (used for linting). Leave empty to auto-generate tags based on library type and directory.

strict.description: Create a library with stricter type checking and build optimization options.

linter.description: The tool to use for running lint checks.

standaloneConfig.description: Split the project configuration into `<projectRoot>/project.json` rather than including it inside `workspace.json`.

setParserOptionsProject.description: Whether or not to configure the ESLint "parserOptions.project" option. We do not do this by default for lint performance reasons.
